questions.prompt: I'm new here. Where can I see the draft you generated? Do I need to download it first?
questions.answer:
You don’t need to download anything first. The draft should appear directly in the Concept Note Builder’s document/editor area, where you can review proposed changes inline.

I can’t verify from the current context whether a draft has already been created. If the editor is blank, the draft may not yet exist; you can ask me to draft or revise a section. Downloads are typically only needed when you want to export the finished version.

questions.prompt: Where do I click to change the funder and funding programme for this note?
questions.answer:
The note is currently linked to:

Funder: European Union LIFE Programme
Funding programme: European City Facility (EUCF) – Call 7

These are changed in the note’s setup/funding selection, not by editing the draft text. I can’t see the interface controls in the current context, so I can’t reliably name the exact button. Look for Back, Project setup, or Funding programme near the top of the Concept Note Builder, then choose a different funder and opportunity.

Note that changing the programme may also change the application template and required sections.

questions.prompt: I have a PDF with more project information. Where do I upload it?
questions.answer:
No PDF is currently attached. In the Concept Note Builder, look for a Sources, Supporting documents, or Add source section, then select Upload document and choose your PDF.

I can’t see your screen, so I can’t confirm the exact button label. If there is no upload option in the editor, return to the note’s setup page and check there. Once uploaded and selected for this note, I can use it as supporting evidence.

questions.prompt: I want to correct a sentence in the draft. Where do I type the change, and how do I save it?
questions.answer:
You have two options:

Edit directly: Click the sentence in the document/editor area and type the correction. I can’t confirm from the available context whether saving is automatic or whether there is a Save button—check the top of the editor for a save/status indicator.

Ask me to revise it: In this chat, write:
“Replace ‘[current sentence]’ with ‘[corrected sentence]’.”
I’ll create an inline proposal. You must then review and accept it in the document controls; the chat request alone does not change the draft.
